div.p: Requester, reviewer and approver are three people. A requester cannot approve their own case. If only two people are available, the case waits; it does not get a shortcut.

ul.li: Fact — has a source. State the source and its as-of date. Without a source it is not a fact, it is Unverified.
Calculation — state the formula, the inputs and the input versions. A number without its inputs cannot be re-derived.
Inference — state the reasoning and its limits.
Recommendation — state what would change your mind.

div.p: Official filing beats licensed vendor beats public commentary. Tag the case with the weakest tier it relies on, not the strongest. A case relying on an unverified source does not enter Approval.
When two sources disagree, record both. Do not silently pick one. The disagreement is itself evidence about confidence.
div.h2: Use of the AI research agent
div.p: The agent drafts, summarises, finds gaps and argues the other side. It does not approve, does not move stages and does not replace a reviewer. Every claim it produces carries a source or is marked Unverified. An agent draft is an input to review, never the review itself.

Market data reaches a case as attached evidence with its own as-of and retrieval timestamps. Data pulled at an unknown time is not evidence. Public sources may inform a case but do not on their own support a controlled decision when policy requires licensed data.
Challenge, dissent, disposition and rationale go in the case chatter. A decision whose reasoning lives in a private channel cannot be audited and is treated as undocumented.

ol.li: Decision requested — the specific action and size.
Evidence — each item with source, as-of date and tier.
Key risks and limits — including position and mandate limits.
What would change our mind — explicit falsifiers.
Missing information — gaps, and whether they block.

div.p: Sections 5, 7 and 8 are not optional. A memo without a counter-thesis or without stated gaps is incomplete regardless of its length.
